title: an assertion that relabels the Clock class as typeof Directory at the capability argument does not make the layer provide Directory; the provide is refused for Directory by name
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Layer Algebra': 'A layer MUST associate each capability's nominal context key with a compatible service instance.' The association is made by the `Layer.succeed(Clock, directory)` CALL — the class object in that argument is what the runtime registry keys on — and `as unknown as typeof Directory` is erased before anything runs. So the layer provides Clock, the body requires Directory, and the only closed answer is refusal naming Directory. WHY THIS CASE EXISTS: it is the CAPABILITY-argument twin of `a-laundering-assertion-does-not-change-which-capability-a-layer-provides`, which launders at the LAYER position and whose own notes name this program as 'a live divergence today ... deliberately left out, because a case for it would have to be marked xfail on the fork'. That divergence was closed on 2026-08-27 and this is the case its sibling could not carry, written now that it needs no marker. **The fork was a FAIL-OPEN here**: it read the asserted checker type, certified the program as fully provided, emitted it, and the program panicked at run time on an unsatisfied Directory requirement because the registry held Clock. The reference already reported `SMITHERS2101` at this exact position, so the two backends disagreed and nothing measured it. WHAT THIS CASE PINS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT: it pins the code, the authored position, and that the refusal names Directory. `messageContains` is declared because the payload IS the promise: code and position alone are satisfied by a refusal naming Clock, and 'Clock is missing' is exactly what a resolver that believed the assertion and then confused the two sets would say. The bare capability name is the smallest fragment carrying it on both backends, which render the row differently (`Directory` versus `{Directory}`), and wording is not the contract. It does NOT pin `SMITHERS2104`: the capability argument is perfectly readable and pins exactly one class — the wrong one — so answering 'opaque' here would be a different and worse diagnosis, and the judge compares the declared set exactly, so a second diagnostic beside this one turns the case red. THE PAIRED POSITIVE CONTROL is `a-type-erased-capability-argument-is-the-same-capability`, whose first two entries are `<any>Directory` and `Directory as any` over a Directory layer and must keep compiling AND RUNNING: a resolver that refuses every assertion at the capability argument turns that case red rather than passing this one for the wrong reason. The direct, wrapped and merged `SMITHERS2101` controls are `layer-provide-missing-a-capability`, `a-wrapped-layer-missing-a-capability-names-it` and `layer-merge-satisfies-both`. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating `messageContains` from `Directory` to `Clock` — the exact payload a resolver that believed the assertion and then confused the two sets would emit, so the mutation is the plausible wrong answer rather than a nonsense one — turns the case red on BOTH backends with the message itself printed: the reference reports `SMITHERS2101@26:20 fires, but its message does not contain "Clock": "Layer.provide is missing Directory"` and the fork the same with `"Layer.provide is missing {Directory}"`. That run is also where the rendering difference recorded above was measured, and it is why the declared fragment is the bare capability name and not the sentence around it. The expectation was restored byte-identically (sha256 3586eeda2da6a4f4c65c049d2aeb3f0edb86b28aee6a472d05fb14fc08509b5d before and after, that digest being this file's content at the moment the mutation ran — this sentence is appended afterwards, so the shipped file necessarily hashes differently). The mutator refuses to run at all unless the case is green on BOTH backends first AND its search string occurs exactly once in the file; both refusals were exercised against this case rather than assumed, because a search string that matches nothing mutates nothing and comes back green.
